comments.body:
The `availableWidth` calculation can become negative when the terminal width is narrow, causing incorrect string slicing behavior. When `availableWidth` is negative (e.g., when `labelText.length + link.length + 7` exceeds `terminalWidth`), the expression `availableWidth - dots.length` produces a large negative number. Passing a negative value to `slice()` slices from the end of the string rather than the beginning, producing unexpected truncation results. **Fix:** Guard against negative or very small values: ```typescript const availableWidth = Math.max( 0, terminalWidth - promptBorderWidth - labelText.length - link.length - 2 ) const descriptionTruncated = availableWidth <= dots.length || description.length <= availableWidth ? description.slice(0, Math.max(0, availableWidth)) : description.slice(0, availableWidth - dots.length) + dots ``` ```suggestion const availableWidth = Math.max( 0, terminalWidth - promptBorderWidth - labelText.length - link.length - 2 // two whitespaces ) const dots = '...' // Worarkound for https://github.com/bombshell-dev/clack/issues/441 const descriptionTruncated = availableWidth <= dots.length || description.length <= availableWidth ? description.slice(0, Math.max(0, availableWidth)) : description.slice(0, availableWidth - dots.length) + dots ``` *Spotted by [Graphite Agent](https://app.graphite.com/diamond/?org=vitejs&ref=ai-review-comment)*



Is this helpful? React 👍 or 👎 to let us know.
@graphite-app Only one `Math.max()` call is enough; update your suggestion.

We think that the description doesn't help users much as the user won't be able to choose the templates only with that description and would need to open the website anyway. We also prefer to avoid maintaining the description.
As a conclusion, we think we should not add the description, but have the links.
We think we should keep this as-is as "(listed first)" and "(listed last)" won't clearly tell which one is the template and which one is the framework.
